READABILITY.evidence: Section headers and FFmpeg cross-reference comments help, but kernel logic uses many single-letter names (t, p, o, s, r/g/b, U/V). Magic constants such as 30189, 19077, 39057361 and 14071 in the lumRange code have no FFmpeg pointer. Python string-patch edits also left comments uneven.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: simd.zig runs past 600 lines (sed 598d). The initFilter port and the swscale_create dispatch are very likely over 100 lines each. Experimental files (.exp/g.zig, .exp/odd.py) were left inside /app/swscale-impl. Scalar and vector paths are duplicated per kernel (halfPacked, tailRow, rgbToUV variants).

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Allocation failures are passed up with try, and swscale_create returns NULL when more than 256 vertical taps are needed. Many unexplained fixed-point magic numbers remain (lumRange constants, -838/2047 clamps, the ±30000 clip). Frames narrower than about 4 px are untested, per the agent's own message.

C6-07-CASE1.evidence: SIMD loops fall back to scalar tails (tailRow, `while (i + 8 <= w)` then a scalar loop). 144 extra odd, mixed, upscale and downscale cases are bit-exact. Very small frames (<4 px) were never tested, and configurations over 256 taps return NULL where FFmpeg would split into two passes.

C6-07-CASE2.evidence: build.zig pins `.cpu_model = .{ .explicit = &std.Target.x86.cpu.x86_64_v3 }`. Shared library swscale_candidate links only libc, exports only the three API functions, and is single-threaded, with precomputation done in swscale_create.
